statement: An employer must take all practicable steps to ensure a relevant employee becomes a member of a registered Mandatory Provident Fund scheme within the permitted period after employment begins — 60 days for an employee who is not a casual employee (Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Ordinance section 7(1) with the 60-day permitted period stated in section 7AA(11) and on the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority's employer pages).
caveat: The permitted period for casual employees is 10 days, the 60 days count by calendar days with an extension where the 60th day is a Saturday or public holiday, exempt persons (including certain overseas-scheme members) sit outside the duty, and the employee's own contributions carry a 30-day contribution holiday while employer contributions run from day one.
